editorial:
Ever wonder how stand-up comedy became the huge deal it is today? You get a front-row seat to that history with this look at Rod Quantock. He is a funny guy who has spent fifty years using jokes to talk about serious stuff like politics and the planet. It feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a chat with a legendary rebel. You will see how he used laughter to wake people up about the dangers of corporate greed and climate change while helping build the comedy scene we all love now.

What really works here is the pacing; it keeps you moving through his life without feeling slow. You will love the old clips and the way he stays honest about his beliefs. While some of the political talk might feel heavy for some, the jokes keep it light. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about people who fight the system. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, or if you are a collector, grab the 4K Blu-ray to keep on your shelf.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing Rod in the present day, still performing and still fighting for the earth. There is no big shock twist, but the emotional payoff comes when you see how his early risks paved the way for today's comedians. It ends with a powerful message that humor is one of the best tools we have to create real change in the world before it is too late.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stand-up comedy and social justice.
